description_full: Vusion S.A. engages in the provision of digitalization solutions for commerce in France, rest of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and the Americas. The company offers computer vision and artificial intelligence (AI) platform, which provides inventory management with automatic monitoring and alerts; retail intelligence software; in-store digital retail media platform for digital campaigns; and IoT cloud platform that tracks, monitors, and manages retail IoT devices. It also provides electronic shelf labels; industrial IoT, an inventory management solution; VusionLive, which connects in-store operations with data-augmented intelligence; and EdgeSense, a shelf-edge rail that integrates centralized communication, precise indoor location, and direct connectivity to bluetooth-enabled devices. In addition, the company offers Vusion Connect that connects devices, data streams, and enterprise system into one cloud system, enabling real-time collaboration between stores, associates, and headquarters; Vusion Intelligence that transforms retail data into real-time insights, predictions, and automated actions; Vusion Retail IoT, which turns the physical store into a living intelligent network; and store operational excellence, local e-commerce, data driven commerce, and retail media and shopper experience solutions. The company was formerly known as VusionGroup S.A. and changed its name to Vusion S.A. in January 2026. Vusion S.A. was founded in 1992 and is headquartered in Nanterre, France.

financial_summary: VUSIONGROUP is a mid-cap technology business with a $2.7B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +36% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 9% cost of capital, a 9-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 28%.

The business throws off $72M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.41× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 1.8% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 41% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

news_headlines.title: VusionGroup (OTCMKTS:SRBEF) Stock Crosses Above 200 Day Moving Average – Here’s Why

sect: Its 7% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.32x its revenue share).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 42% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 9% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 35% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 55% and a beta of 0.84, it moves roughly with the market.
Trading is thin (about $34K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 0% in the 2020 crash and 7% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 48% below its DCF fair value of $311, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 3%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $193 to $522 (P10-P90).
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on P/E 8.8 vs 27.4 and EV/EBITDA 12.3 vs 17.1, richer on P/FCF 38.1 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.6% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The Street target $204 on average, 26% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 2.5% annual cash-flow growth, 13pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 8.8% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.56).
It runs a 28% gross margin and converts 4% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.41x.
ROE of 32% is amplified by 3.5x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
SG&A jumped 24% last year, worth watching.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $471.3M.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 36.5% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 71% of profits supports about 12.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Analysts expect 13.1% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 40.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 28%.
Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-1.8%), diluting holders.
people: With about 1,200 employees, each generates about $1.4M of revenue, 3.6x the Technology median.
That works out to $60K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $914K (1x revenue per employee).
